Works from the first frame with or without dithering, no master dark needed. Complements outlier rejection, which handles transients like cosmic rays and satellite trails.
In astrophotography, dithering means shi: In astrophotography, dithering means shifting your telescope's aim by a few random pixels between exposures. This tiny random movement lets your stacking software tell real sky objects apart from camera flaws, for a cleaner, sharper final image.
Dead or overly bright pixels stay in the: Dead or overly bright pixels stay in the exact same spot on the sensor, but the stars move when you dither. Stacking software sees the stuck pixels as errors and rejects them.
Without dithering, thermal noise can lin: Without dithering, thermal noise can line up into ugly vertical or diagonal streaks (worm-like patterns) across the stacked image.
Shifting the sensor across many frames l: Shifting the sensor across many frames lets the computer average out small differences in pixel sensitivity.
